question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3(x+2y)}{2}, & \,0\le y\le x\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Find $P(X<\frac{2}{5}\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{5}).$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(Y\in A\,|\,X=x)={\int }_{A}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}y,
$$

where ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y.$ 

Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{y}^{1}\frac{3(x+2y)}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{y}^{1}(x+2y)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+2xy]}_{x=y}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(\frac{1}{2}+2y-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}-2{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}[\frac{1+4y-5{y}^{2}}{2}] \\  & =\frac{3(1+4y-5{y}^{2})}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3(1+4y-5{y}^{2})}{4}, & \,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)}.
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $0\le y\le x\le 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3(x+2y)}{2})}{(\frac{3(1+4y-5{y}^{2})}{4})} \\  & =\frac{2(x+2y)}{1+4y-5{y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2(x+2y)}{1+4y-5{y}^{2}}, & \,0\le y\le x\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute our probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<\frac{2}{5}\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{5}) & ={\int }_{y}^{2/5}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y=\frac{1}{5})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/5}^{2/5}\frac{2(x+2(\frac{1}{5}))}{(1+4(\frac{1}{5})-5{(\frac{1}{5})}^{2})}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/5}^{2/5}\frac{2(x+\frac{2}{5})}{(\frac{8}{5})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{1/5}^{2/5}(5x+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[\frac{5{x}^{2}}{2}+2x]}_{1/5}^{2/5} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\frac{2}{5}+\frac{4}{5}-\frac{1}{10}-\frac{2}{5}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\frac{7}{10}) \\  & =\frac{7}{40}.\end{aligned}
$$
